newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Dostum pilots defect to Afghan mutineers in jets.
newsitem.headline: Dostum pilots defect to Afghan mutineers in jets.

text.p: Three fighter jets belonging to northern Afghan opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum were flown by turncoats to his mutinous former second-in-command on Saturday, an Islamic Taleban militia spokesman said.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Wakeel Ahmed from the southern Afghan city of Kandahar as saying three jets were flown from the airport at Dostum-controlled Mazar-i-Sharif.
Ahmed said one landed at Kabul airport while the other two first bombed the airport in the northwestern town of Shibarghan, capital of Jozjan province and a Dostum stronghold.
They then landed at an airport in Maimana, capital of Faryab province, which is held by Dostum's former foreign minister and deputy, General Abdul Malik, said Ahmed.
Malik on Monday switched his allegiance to Dostum's enemies, the Taleban.
Ahmed said the two jets were commanded by General Hafeez-ullah, a key Dostum officer now in league with the mutineers.
Malik is apparently acting in collusion with the purist Taleban that control the capital Kabul and most of the rest of Afghanistan.
Dostum, leader of an anti-Taleban alliance that includes factions loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, had been battling the militant Islamic warriors inconclusively for months.
